REKLAMO VS. NAGPROTESTA?

Tinitingnan ng pulisya ang posibleng paghahain ng reklamo laban sa mga nagprotesta sa harap ng St. Gerrard Construction compound ng mga Discaya sa Pasig City.

"Identified po 'yung grupo at saka 'yung leaders. We are preparing the necessary charges against them in coordination sa pamilya Discaya," sabi ni National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) Dir. P/Maj. Gen. Anthony Aberin.

"It was not covered by a permit... Hindi po natin sila inabutan dahil lightning protest po 'yun. Kung inabutan po natin sila, aarestuhin po natin sila," giit ni Aberin.

data.text:
The recent admission by Health Secretary Ted Herbosa—that he does not know where the remaining ₱89.9 billion PhilHealth funds went after being transferred to the National Treasury in 2024—is more than a bureaucratic oversight. 

It is a glaring symptom of a deeper, systemic failure within the Department of Health (DOH) and its stewardship of public health resources.

At the heart of this issue is a breakdown in fiscal oversight. The DOH, under whose umbrella PhilHealth operates, should have clear visibility over such a massive fund transfer. 

Herbosa’s lack of knowledge suggests either poor coordination with the Department of Finance (DOF) or a failure to assert accountability over health-dedicated funds. In either case, the result is the same: public money, meant to serve the sick and vulnerable, has vanished into a bureaucratic fog.

This misstep also reveals a troubling misalignment with the goals of the Universal Health Care (UHC) Law. Designed to expand access and reduce out-of-pocket costs, the UHC Law is a cornerstone of health equity in the Philippines. Redirecting PhilHealth’s unused subsidies—without reinvesting them into health programs—undermines this mandate. As Congressman Chel Diokno rightly pointed out, these funds could have broadened PhilHealth’s benefit packages, reaching more patients in need of dialysis, cardiac care, and other essential services.

Legal and ethical questions now surround the transfer. The Supreme Court is reviewing petitions that challenge its constitutionality. If the funds were appropriated for health, using them elsewhere may constitute technical malversation. This is not merely a budgetary concern—it is a matter of justice and integrity.

Perhaps most concerning is the leadership gap exposed during congressional hearings. Herbosa’s admission that he “does not know exactly” where the funds went raises serious doubts about his command of the agency’s financial operations. Leadership in public health demands not just medical expertise, but fiscal vigilance. When billions are at stake, ignorance is not an excuse—it is a breach of public trust.

Several factors contributed to this failure. There was a lack of inter-agency transparency, with DOH and DOF appearing disconnected on fund utilization. Internal controls within PhilHealth were weak, failing to safeguard its budget or ensure strategic use. Communication to stakeholders—including Congress, civil society, and health workers—was poor. Most critically, there was a failure to prioritize health needs. Funds meant to alleviate suffering were diverted or frozen, leaving patients and providers in limbo.

quoted_tweet.text:
Master inquisitor Congressman Chel Diokno asked DOH Secretary Ted Herbosa where the diverted PhilHealth funds went to.

Herbosa said it was the Department of Finance that knows where it went to - and then gave the weirdest justification that it probably went to infrastructure projects related to health.

“I requested the DOF na gamitin sana for health projects like infrastructure… building of a road actually allows a patient to access health care faster… even bridges actually.”

That is a disgusting justification and logic.

Let’s not forget accountability for the PhilHealth funds that was diverted - funds that could have been used to give more Filipinos zero billing in hospitals.

Pag binayaran ng gobyerno ang hospital bill for cancer or other sicknesses, less or zero corruption ang pwede nilang gawin.

Pero pag infra, alam natin na gutom na gutom ang mga Congressmen and Senators for infra projects dahil pwedeng pwede makurakot - pag ghost project eh 100% kurakot.

Kaya todo budget insertions and dagdag bawas ang Congress sa budgets ng Dep Ed and PhilHealth para lang madagdagan ang sa DPWH.

Nakakasuka!

Buti na lang andyan ulet si Cong. Chel Diokno who quietly but surely leads any resource person to spill out the truth.

Parang yung pag tanong nya kay Lawrence Lubiano na umamin sa 30 Million donation.

Another master class in cross examination.

#ChelDiokno
#BudgetHearing
